reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    State: Alabama
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for material breach?

    Primary statute encoded:
    - AL Code  35-9A-421 (2021), especially subsections (a) and (d).
*/

% -----------------------
% Scenario facts (question)
% -----------------------

state(alabama).
focus_year(2021).

landlord(l1).
tenant(t1).

/*
  We encode the factual statement as a concrete scenario:
  - Tenant committed a "material noncompliance" (material breach).
  - Landlord delivered a proper written 7-business-day notice to terminate.
  - Tenant attempted and adequately completed a cure within the allowed time.
  - No noncurable default applies; cure-limit not exceeded; no intentional misrepresentation.
*/

% The breach at issue is a material noncompliance with the rental agreement.
breach(b1).
breach_type(b1, material_noncompliance).   % corresponds to 35-9A-421(a) "material noncompliance"
breach_actor(b1, t1).

% The landlord delivered a written notice to terminate for this breach.
notice(n1).
notice_for_breach(n1, b1).
notice_delivered_by(n1, l1).
notice_delivered_to(n1, t1).
notice_is_written(n1).
notice_specifies_acts_and_omissions(n1).
notice_specifies_termination(n1).
notice_receipt_day(n1, 0).                % day 0 = receipt day (relative timeline)
notice_termination_day(n1, 8).            % termination day at least 7 business days after receipt

% Tenant's cure attempt and adequacy.
cure_attempt(c1).
cure_for_breach(c1, b1).
cure_by_tenant(c1, t1).
cure_completed_day(c1, 5).                % cured before termination date and within the 7-day window
cure_is_adequate(c1).

% Limits/consent facts relevant to 35-9A-421(d).
cures_in_last_12_months(t1, 1).
landlord_express_written_consent_to_additional_cure(l1, t1, no).

% Facts negating noncurable defaults / misrepresentation.
intentional_misrepresentation_in_agreement_or_application(t1, no).

% No noncurable default act occurred (drugs, illegal firearm, criminal assault, etc.).
noncurable_default_act_occurred(t1, no).

% No "substantially same breach within six months after prior notice-and-cure" situation.
repeat_same_breach_within_6_months(t1, no).



% -----------------------------------------
% Scenario helper predicate required by spec
% -----------------------------------------

scenario_statement :-
    state(alabama),
    focus_year(2021),
    landlord(l1),
    tenant(t1),
    breach(b1),
    breach_type(b1, material_noncompliance),
    breach_actor(b1, t1),
    notice(n1),
    notice_for_breach(n1, b1),
    notice_delivered_by(n1, l1),
    notice_delivered_to(n1, t1),
    notice_is_written(n1),
    notice_specifies_acts_and_omissions(n1),
    notice_specifies_termination(n1),
    notice_receipt_day(n1, ReceiptDay),
    notice_termination_day(n1, TermDay),
    ReceiptDay =:= 0,
    TermDay >= 7, % at least seven business days after receipt per 35-9A-421(a)
    cure_attempt(c1),
    cure_for_breach(c1, b1),
    cure_by_tenant(c1, t1),
    cure_completed_day(c1, CureDay),
    cure_is_adequate(c1),
    CureDay >= ReceiptDay,
    CureDay =< TermDay,
    intentional_misrepresentation_in_agreement_or_application(t1, no),
    noncurable_default_act_occurred(t1, no),
    repeat_same_breach_within_6_months(t1, no).



% ----------------------------
% Statute encoding (deterministic)
% ----------------------------

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(a) (2021):
   - For material noncompliance (and other specified noncompliances), landlord may give written notice.
   - Notice termination date must be not less than seven business days after receipt.
   - If breach is adequately remedied before the date specified, rental agreement shall not terminate.
*/
statute_421a_notice_valid_for_material_noncompliance(Notice) :-
    notice(Notice),
    notice_is_written(Notice),
    notice_specifies_acts_and_omissions(Notice),
    notice_specifies_termination(Notice),
    notice_receipt_day(Notice, ReceiptDay),
    notice_termination_day(Notice, TermDay),
    TermDay - ReceiptDay >= 7.

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(a) (2021):
   "An intentional misrepresentation ... may not be remedied or cured."
*/
statute_421a_misrepresentation_is_incurable(Tenant) :-
    intentional_misrepresentation_in_agreement_or_application(Tenant, yes).

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(d) (2021):
   - No breach may be cured more than two times in any 12-month period
     except by the express written consent of the landlord.
*/
statute_421d_cure_limit_blocks_cure(Tenant) :-
    cures_in_last_12_months(Tenant, N),
    N >= 2.

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(d) (2021):
   - Certain acts/omissions are noncurable defaults; tenant has no right to remedy unless landlord consents.
   We model this as scenario-level booleans for simplicity.
*/
statute_421d_noncurable_default_applies(Tenant) :-
    noncurable_default_act_occurred(Tenant, yes).

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(d)(4) (2021):
   - Repeat substantially same breach within 6 months after prior notice-and-cure is noncurable.
*/
statute_421d_repeat_same_breach_within_6_months_is_noncurable(Tenant) :-
    repeat_same_breach_within_6_months(Tenant, yes).

/* AL Code  35-9A-421(d) (2021):
   - Tenant has no right to remedy such a noncurable default unless landlord consents.
*/
statute_421d_landlord_consented_to_extra_cure(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    landlord_express_written_consent_to_additional_cure(Landlord, Tenant, yes).

/* Determine whether this tenant has a statutory "right to cure" this breach under 35-9A-421,
   i.e., whether landlord must treat a timely adequate cure as preventing termination.
*/
statute_tenant_has_right_to_cure(Landlord, Tenant, Breach) :-
    breach(Breach),
    breach_actor(Breach, Tenant),
    breach_type(Breach, material_noncompliance),        % question asks "material breach"
    \+ statute_421a_misrepresentation_is_incurable(Tenant),
    (
        % If cure-limit not exceeded, OK; if exceeded, need express written consent.
        ( \+ statute_421d_cure_limit_blocks_cure(Tenant) )
        ;
        statute_421d_landlord_consented_to_extra_cure(Landlord, Tenant)
    ),
    % Noncurable defaults block any right to remedy unless landlord consents.
    (
        ( \+ statute_421d_noncurable_default_applies(Tenant),
          \+ statute_421d_repeat_same_breach_within_6_months_is_noncurable(Tenant)
        )
        ;
        statute_421d_landlord_consented_to_extra_cure(Landlord, Tenant)
    ).

/* 35-9A-421(a) (2021): cure is effective if tenant adequately remedies before the date specified in notice.
   We also require a valid statutory notice (written, specifies acts, termination date >= 7 business days).
*/
statute_cure_is_effective_for_notice(Landlord, Tenant, Breach, Notice, CureAttempt) :-
    statute_tenant_has_right_to_cure(Landlord, Tenant, Breach),
    notice_for_breach(Notice, Breach),
    statute_421a_notice_valid_for_material_noncompliance(Notice),
    cure_for_breach(CureAttempt, Breach),
    cure_by_tenant(CureAttempt, Tenant),
    cure_is_adequate(CureAttempt),
    notice_receipt_day(Notice, ReceiptDay),
    notice_termination_day(Notice, TermDay),
    cure_completed_day(CureAttempt, CureDay),
    CureDay >= ReceiptDay,
    CureDay =< TermDay.

/* Derived duty question: Must landlord accept tenant's attempt to cure?
   We treat "must accept" as: if tenant completes an adequate timely cure within statutory parameters,
   the lease shall not terminate for that breach; thus landlord cannot refuse the cure for purposes of termination.
*/
landlord_must_accept_cure(Landlord, Tenant, Breach) :-
    notice(N),
    cure_attempt(C),
    statute_cure_is_effective_for_notice(Landlord, Tenant, Breach, N, C).



% ----------------------------
% Final answer predicate
% ----------------------------

housing_answer(Result) :-
    scenario_statement,
    landlord(l1),
    tenant(t1),
    breach(b1),
    ( landlord_must_accept_cure(l1, t1, b1) ->
        Result = yes
    ;
        Result = no
    ),
    !.



% ----------------------------
% Main entrypoint (required)
% ----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for material breach?
